newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end higher, trim gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end higher, trim gains.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures cut gains late but still ended moderately to sharply higher.
A strong close in U.S. Treasury bond futures, which upticked to finish moderately higher and near the day's peaks, plus a further push upward in the U.S. dollar, undergirded stock index futures.
Traders reported dealer activity picked up again late, with firms seen selling futures in choppy trading as they prepared for a glut of U.S. economic data that starts Tuesday.
Some brokers expressed surprise that stock index futures managed to keep the bulk of daily gains scored at midmorning.
"I thought we were going to give some of this (rise) back by the end of the day," said one floor analyst. "There's no reason for this to be either way (up or down)."
A strong performance in Nasdaq indices helped buoy stock index futures.

The analyst said the gains resulted partly from technical resilience after June S&P 500s bounced up from a brief morning pullback, along with signs that month-end position adjustment may have begun early.
"I think we are getting some month-end stuff early," he said.
"We could be seeing some cash inflows to mutual funds," agreed a floor broker.
The analyst also said the ability of June S&P 500s to bounce up from a retracement level at 767.00 and to recover above Friday's low at 767.50 contributed to the rise.

Tuesday's first-quarter U.S. employment cost index is expected to rise 0.9 percent after a 0.8 percent rise in the previous report. March durable goods orders are seen flat, with a 0.1-percent dip exclusive of defense orders.
Traders will also watch for comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan Tuesday at the IMF/World Bank meeting.
